failure_reason: Akamai bot-management returns HTTP 403 'Restricted Access' on every /shop/* PLP URL tested, confirmed independently across all 3 access tiers: (1) curl_cffi with Chrome-120 TLS impersonation, both cold and with a warmed session (homepage cookies + same-origin Referer/Sec-Fetch headers); (2) Playwright, both headless Chromium and headful real-Chrome channel; (3) a live Claude-in-Chrome browser session (navigating from the already-loaded, working homepage). All three returned the same 'Pottery Barn Kids: 403 - Restricted Access' page. Only the homepage (/), /robots.txt, the sitemap XML files under /netstorage/sitemaps/, and /llms.txt (all outside /shop/) returned HTTP 200. This matches the prior Furniture-pass note for this company (archive c5) exactly. r.jina.ai / translate.goog / archive.org were not used per this task's rules, so no PLP content or product count could be verified this pass.
notes: 'New' is the site's dedicated Secondary Navigation item -> https://www.potterybarnkids.com/shop/new/. llms.txt confirms this page's own title is 'New Arrivals: Kids & Baby' with description 'Find the latest trends and collections for babies, toddlers, and kids. Discover what's new this season' -- this directly confirms a genuine New Arrivals concept (explicit 'New Arrivals' wording), not merely a themed 'New Collection' campaign name. Sitemap enumeration of shop-sitemap-1.xml.gz under /shop/new/* surfaced a rich genuine substructure: an 'all-new' rollup, three age-segment rollups explicitly named '...-new-arrivals' (all-kids-new-arrivals, all-baby-new-arrivals, all-toddler-new-arrivals -- strongest signal), ~15 department-level 'new-X' listings, seasonal children (holiday-new, new-easter, new-halloween, thanksgiving-new, new-st-patricks-day), and 'new-in-stock' (kept but flagged ambiguous). Excluded as non-merchandising: /shop/new/test-shop-path-cio/, test-all-products/, test-shop-path/, secret-all-products/ (internal QA/staging paths, not customer-facing). Because every /shop/new/* URL returned Akamai 403 on all 3 access tiers, no page could be opened to confirm it is a real product grid vs. an editorial/campaign page per the brief's 'Collection' test -- so every row below carries a combined flag: qty unverifiable AND genuine-PLP status unconfirmed, recorded from site-owned nav/sitemap/llms.txt evidence only.
